selection_basis: Exclude all previously used task identities: Jinja1621, Click2800, dirty-equals43, Llama17070, HF3997 and Pillow68.
Prefer clear, bounded Python requirements and variation between shared-function changes and more separate stages or API layers.
Use only public feature requirements, Dockerfile/setup/runner declarations and read-only registry architecture information; no solution, hidden test or model outcomes.

selected_tasks.description: DSPy organizes language-model programs. Parse Python-style tool-call text safely, and separately coerce tool arguments before schema validation.
requirements: A public AST-only parser normalizes top-level keyword-only calls containing literals into tool_calls, preserving order without executing code.
Before Tool validation, schema-guided coercion handles string numbers, booleans, durations and sizes while preserving string-typed fields.
selected_tasks.explicit: Both requirements name tool.py; feature 2 targets ToolCalls.validate_input/parse_python_calls and feature 3 targets Tool._validate_and_parse_args/coerce_args.
selected_tasks.inference: The stages can compose when parsed calls are passed to Tool, but parsing itself is not responsible for execution. Shared imports/helpers may still overlap.
limits: Relatively separate functions, not disjoint files.
Integer schemas with fractional duration values require care; no additional acceptance rule is invented.
environment_risks: Python 3.11 with substantial DSPy dev dependencies.
Dockerfile pins litellm 1.77.1; verify actual image and evaluation without real model calls.

feature_evidence.requirement_summary: A public AST-only parser normalizes top-level keyword-only calls containing literals into tool_calls, preserving order without executing code.
Before Tool validation, schema-guided coercion handles string numbers, booleans, durations and sizes while preserving string-typed fields.

selected_tasks.description: Outlines builds prompts from templates. Add per-template custom filters and a reusable global filter registry.
requirements: prompt and Prompt.from_str/from_file accept filters, with create_jinja_env centralizing registration.
register_filter/unregister_filter manage global filters; local filters explicitly take precedence over global filters.
selected_tasks.explicit: Both name prompts.py and feature 2 explicitly defines local-over-global precedence.
selected_tasks.inference: Environment creation, local argument plumbing and registry state must be integrated consistently.
limits: Lifetime semantics for already-created Prompt objects after registry changes are not fully specified.
Same-file changes do not prove merge conflicts will occur.
environment_risks: Python 3.11; test extras may introduce substantial model-related dependencies.
The task concerns template processing and declares no GPU or model API requirement; package imports still need validation.

feature_evidence.requirement_summary: prompt and Prompt.from_str/from_file accept filters, with create_jinja_env centralizing registration.
register_filter/unregister_filter manage global filters; local filters explicitly take precedence over global filters.

selected_tasks.description: Click builds command-line programs. Let click.edit pass extra editor arguments and choose the editor process working directory.
requirements: editor_args are inserted between the editor command and filename with proper shell quoting; default None preserves existing behavior.
working_dir passes through the public edit API and underlying editor launch; default None, with errors for invalid/inaccessible directories.
selected_tasks.explicit: Both requirements name the public termui API and underlying Editor implementation.
selected_tasks.inference: Independent parameters must both survive the API/constructor/subprocess chain; interaction is cross-layer plumbing rather than one algorithm.
limits: The filename interpretation when a relative filename and working_dir are combined is not fully specified.
A Linux headless run cannot establish behavior for GUI editors or Windows.
environment_risks: Python 3.11 and relatively small dependency set.
Use a noninteractive stand-in editor for environment checks; avoid launching a GUI or waiting for user interaction.

feature_evidence.requirement_summary: editor_args are inserted between the editor command and filename with proper shell quoting; default None preserves existing behavior.
working_dir passes through the public edit API and underlying editor launch; default None, with errors for invalid/inaccessible directories.

selected_tasks.description: Jinja renders templates. Add case-insensitive grouping and descending group order to groupby, including its async path.
requirements: case_sensitive defaults to False; normalized keys govern sorting/grouping, while the first item supplies the displayed key spelling.
reverse defaults to False and allows descending group order.
selected_tasks.explicit: Both modify filters.py groupby; feature 1 explicitly includes synchronous and asynchronous variants.
selected_tasks.inference: Case normalization and reverse must use a consistent sorting key in the same grouping pipeline.
limits: The new default case_sensitive=False changes older grouping behavior; do not repeat the broad backward-compatibility claim as unchanged output.
A short implementation may finish before both agents have unsubmitted code; checkpoint feasibility remains unverified.
environment_risks: Python 3.11 and small dependency set; no GPU or external service declared.
Both sync and async entry points need environment validation.

feature_evidence.requirement_summary: case_sensitive defaults to False; normalized keys govern sorting/grouping, while the first item supplies the displayed key spelling.

next_validation_policy: After selection is frozen, reference/tests may be used only for evaluator environment checks, never exposed to agents.

Report combined reference compatibility separately; do not replace tasks based on scores or repair answers.
An ARM64 registry manifest is not proof of a working runtime; separately record actual image ID, base, baked runner and scores.
limits: All four groups still come from one benchmark, CooperBench.
